clue.text: Daughter by cliff-face rocks writing

indicators.note: 'by' means next to, so the daughter's letter is set beside the rocks

parts.note: scree is the loose rock fragments that collect below a cliff face
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A daughter sits beside the fallen rocks under a cliff, scribbling away.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long, often tedious piece of writing, so the noun 'writing' covers it as a broader term.

clue.text: Goldfinches about to come to grief

parts.note: C stands for circa, the Latin for about with dates
grief in the old sense of trouble or injury is harm

explanation.surface: Some goldfinches are about to meet a sad end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come to' only links the pieces. The definition relies on collective nouns: a group of goldfinches is called a charm.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for a flock of these birds is a charm, so the plural names the group.

clue.text: Coming to finish, see ace run freely, demonstrating staying power

parts.note: the finish of something is its end

indicators.note: running freely means moving without a fixed course, so these letters are rearranged at will

explanation.surface: A runner nears the line, watching an ace race freely, showing stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming to', 'see' and 'demonstrating' are only link words padding the surface; the anagram indicator is 'freely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the ability to keep going under strain, which is exactly staying power.

clue.text: Vessel has a name inscribed in a foreign language

indicators.note: something inscribed in an object is written into it, so these letters go inside the vessel word

parts.note: a dish is a vessel for serving food

explanation.surface: A boat bears a name lettered in another tongue on its hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a serving dish; 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish is the tongue spoken in Denmark, so to an English speaker it is a foreign language.

clue.text: This person in shock, I suspect, is longing to be elsewhere

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the person goes inside the jumbled letters
something suspect is dubious or not what it seems, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: the setter referring to themself is 'me'

explanation.surface: Someone in a state of shock declares themselves eager to be anywhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like a noun or verb about crime, but it is the anagram signal; 'in' places the setter inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being homesick means pining for your own home while away, a yearning to be in another place.

clue.text: Be slightly deranged and need to go up on the roof?

definitions.meaning: an informal British idiom for being a bit mad

definitions.text: need to go up on the roof?
definitions.meaning: taken literally, a dislodged roof tile calls for a climb to fix it

explanation.surface: Someone a little crazy who also needs a roofer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mildly unhinged; read literally it describes a roof missing a secure tile.

clue.text: Loan gives male good time — nothing right in that

indicators.note: 'in that' says the next letters go inside what has just been built

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A borrowing scheme promises a man fun, but there's nothing correct about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' is a link word; O and RT go into MGAGE just after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortgage is a loan secured on property, usually to buy a home.

clue.text: Set up talks on reducing arms, in short

definitions.meaning: to set up a venture is to launch or begin it

definitions.text: talks on reducing arms, in short
definitions.meaning: the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty negotiations between the USA and USSR were known by an acronym

explanation.surface: Arranging negotiations to cut weapons, briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up a business is to begin it; the acronym names the 1991 arms-reduction treaty talks.

clue.text: Person sending things? Tricks to disregard for the most part

parts.note: cons are swindles or tricks

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter is kept

parts.note: to ignore something is to disregard it

explanation.surface: Who sends packages? Mostly ignore the swindles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the last letter of IGNORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A consignor is the party who dispatches goods to a recipient, so a sender of things.

clue.text: Girl gone to find success in a particular field

parts.note: a maiden is a girl or young unmarried woman
something gone is finished, over

explanation.surface: A young woman departs to seek her fortune in some chosen area of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'particular field' is a cricket field: a maiden over is six balls bowled with no runs scored, a triumph for the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, bowling an over that concedes no runs is an achievement on the pitch.

clue.text: Composer showing merit, first to last

indicators.note: the instruction takes the opening letter and shifts it to the end

parts.note: to merit a reward is to earn it

explanation.surface: A composer proves deserving, leading from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' is a link word. Thomas Arne was the English composer of 'Rule, Britannia!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne was an 18th-century English composer, so he is an example of the category.

clue.text: I'm so excited with a bar offering wonderful food

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by a bar serving marvellous dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two sets of fodder; 'excited' rearranges IMSOABAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, hence any delicious fare.

clue.text: The distinctive style with which we introduce our newspaper

definitions.text: The distinctive style with which we introduce our newspaper

parts.words: The distinctive style with which we introduce our newspaper
parts.note: the Daily Telegraph masthead at the top of the front page is printed in blackletter type

explanation.surface: The paper describing the look of its own front-page title.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackletter typeface of the masthead is called by the same name as the medieval architectural style.

clue.text: Set down passage to be read out

indicators.note: something read out is spoken, so we want a word with the same sound

parts.note: a lane is a narrow passage or way

explanation.surface: A passage is put down in writing, ready to be recited.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past participles: something that has lain has been placed or resting down.

clue.text: Lincoln rector originally managed church going in the wrong direction

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of US president Abraham Lincoln

indicators.note: the original letter of a word is its first

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A rector in Lincoln once ran a church that went astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' suggests the English cathedral city, but it is the president.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrance means straying from the normal path, a deviation in the wrong direction.

clue.text: Coming down to provide illumination

definitions.meaning: a bird or plane settling on something is said to light on it
lamps and bulbs installed give a room its light

explanation.surface: Descending in order to shed light.
explanation.definitionFit: Landing (as a bird alights) and the illumination of a room share this word.

clue.text: Speed isn't bad? There's less than total enthusiasm

indicators.note: bad here means spoiled or wrong, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Going fast isn't wicked, says someone not fully committed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' is a link word; 'bad' rearranges SPEEDISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lukewarm about something is a lack of full eagerness, half-hearted feeling.

clue.text: Worthy archbishop joining bishop in drink

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I

indicators.note: 'in' puts the bishop inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A deserving archbishop meets a bishop over a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Something praiseworthy deserves credit, so it is worthy.

clue.text: Maybe ghost getting to storm angrily around flat

indicators.note: 'around' says the first part surrounds the second

parts.note: to rant is to rage or storm in fury
a flat surface is even

explanation.surface: A ghost, perhaps, whirls angrily round an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but means level; 'getting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A revenant is one returned from the dead; a ghost is an example, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Leave social event that finishes early

indicators.note: a word that ends early loses its last letter

parts.note: a party is a social gathering

explanation.surface: Depart from a gathering that wraps up ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To part from someone is to leave them or go away.

clue.text: Get better sort of truck

definitions.meaning: things improving are said to perk up or recover

explanation.surface: An improving style of lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is the phrasal verb; the same term names a small open-backed truck.

clue.text: Walked with head invisible, being bent

indicators.note: a word whose head cannot be seen loses its first letter

parts.note: marched means walked in step

explanation.surface: Someone walked with their head lowered out of view, stooping.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved back or bow shape is bent, the form of an arch.

clue.text: Monster lurking in filthy drains

indicators.note: something lurking is concealed inside, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A beast hides in dirty sewers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra was the many-headed serpent of Greek myth slain by Heracles.

clue.text: Relinquished and put into store

definitions.meaning: giving up a position or arms is surrendering them
good wine is stored in a cellar to mature

explanation.surface: Given up and stored away.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrendering arms or office uses this phrase, as does cellaring wine to mature.

clue.text: Ram, the first thing you see on Welsh border

indicators.text: the first thing you see on
indicators.note: the first thing seen of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a border is an edge

explanation.surface: A sheep is the first sight on the Welsh border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ram' looks like a male sheep, but it is the verb meaning to force in.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram something into a gap is to jam or force it in tightly.

clue.text: Woman to have a meal sent back

indicators.note: sending a word back reads it from right to left

parts.note: to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: A woman returns her dinner to the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female given name, as in the author Blyton.

clue.text: Impede leaders viewed as idiots

parts.note: to block something is to obstruct it
heads are leaders of organisations

explanation.surface: Obstruct bosses considered to be fools.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolt has a head like a lump of wood, so the plural means fools.

clue.text: Asian person seen wandering across enclosure

indicators.note: 'across' says the jumbled letters span either side of the enclosure
wandering letters stray from their places, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a pale is a fenced area, as in 'beyond the pale'

explanation.surface: An Asian traveller is spotted roaming over a fenced field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' jumbles the fodder, and 'across' splits that jumble so its halves sit either side of the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Nepal, the Himalayan country, is an Asian person.

clue.text: Notice someone using a red box?

definitions.meaning: a printed notice put up on a wall
British pillar boxes for mail are red, so whoever puts letters in one is sending them

explanation.surface: A notice about someone at a red letterbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard on a wall is one sense; one who mails letters in a British pillar box is the other.
